newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Cullen says NZ ManFed report "dangerous beat up".
newsitem.headline: Cullen says NZ ManFed report "dangerous beat up".

text.p: Opposition Labour finance spokesman Michael Cullen said on Friday that a Bankers Trust report commissioned by the Manufacturers Federation did not live up to ManFed's claims.

"ManFed claims the report shows that cutting government spending by $1 billion could bring the TWI back by four percent and see interest rates fall by two percent. That is a beat up and a dangerous beat up," Cullen said in a statement.

"In fact careful reading of the document shows that even if government spending were slashed by NZ$1 billion this would be likely to have an impact on the exchange rate of no more than one or two percent -- this is less than the variation which has occurred since the election."
Cullen said the report supported Labour's argument that a further fiscal tightening would need at some stage to be followed by an easing because it did not make sense to run ever larger surpluses.

"Knocking $1 billion off social services, which would in fact be the area most likely to bear the brunt of such a cut, is a huge price to pay for a much smaller impact on the exchange rate than could be achieved by intelligent action on the part of the government," Cullen said.
